The temporal-spatial game state parser extracts structured data from HTML tables, mapping each game row to a temporal event with associated spread and ATS outcome. The kickoff time inference engine extends this by extracting precise kickoff times, enabling body-clock modeling. The ATS outcome validator ensures that spread-based predictions are verified against actual outcomes. These primitives form a dual system where parsing provides the data layer and validation ensures fidelity. Failure modes include misalignment between parsed rows and harness data, incorrect attribution of spreads, or missing kickoff times. The system's robustness depends on consistent schema adherence and cross-validation.
